title: Directus CMS Integration
description:
## Overview

Integrate Directus into the Astro template as an optional build-time CMS path so future sites can start Directus-ready without losing the template's local-first developer experience. The integration should reduce repeated CMS wiring while preserving clean builds when no Directus environment variables are configured.

## Architecture

The integration follows a Content Provider pattern: pages call a unified API such as `getBlogPosts()` and `getLocations()` without knowing whether content came from Directus, cache, or local template content. The provider selects the source per content area using a CMS-preferred fallback chain: Live Directus -> Disk Cache -> Local Content/Fixtures.

Key architectural decisions:

1. Pre-render CMS markdown in provider/normalization code; pages never import raw Directus modules.
2. Use CMS-preferred fallback per collection or content area, independently.
3. Keep Directus optional for local development and template previews; only fail hard when `DIRECTUS_REQUIRED=true`.
4. Use Astro native remote image support instead of custom image download code.
5. Use a custom `rehype-sanitize` schema for CMS markdown security.
6. Validate cache entries against `DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG` to prevent cross-site content contamination.

## Scope

- Directus-backed content in this bead set: `blog_articles`, `blog_categories`, and `cities` mapped to Locations.
- Existing local content remains the offline fallback where available.
- Team and Services stay local-only unless new beads deliberately expand the scope.
- Row-level multi-tenancy uses `site.slug` filtering.
- Public planning text, committed docs, logs, cache metadata, and build artifacts must not expose private Directus hosts, tokens, credentials, or infrastructure hints.

## Plan Gate

Before Phase 1 implementation starts, complete `astro-template-directus-integration-rb2.7.1` so the checked-in PRD and this bead plan agree. If `prd/PRD.md` is the intended source of truth instead, revise this bead tree before implementation.

## Authoritative Reference

- Current implementation source of truth: this Directus bead tree after Phase 0 reconciliation.
- Checked-in PRD: must be reconciled by `astro-template-directus-integration-rb2.7.1`.
- Reference implementation: `arp-astro`, to be inspected for transferable patterns rather than copied blindly.
- Directus connection details: configured only through environment variables and private deployment notes, never committed public text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Phase 0 is closed before Phase 1 implementation work begins.
- The completed integration preserves no-Directus local builds and previews by default.
- Directus strict mode fails clearly only when `DIRECTUS_REQUIRED=true`.
- No secrets, tokens, concrete Directus instance URLs, or sensitive infrastructure hints are committed, logged, cached in public output, or emitted in build artifacts.
- The final implementation has lint, typecheck, tests, build verification, and token-leak audit coverage appropriate to the touched surface.

title: Phase 1: DX & Config Foundation
description:
## Overview

Foundation phase: developer-facing configuration that every subsequent phase builds on. Sets up environment variable patterns, image handling, diagnostic logging, and gitignore rules. This is intentionally small and self-contained — it can be reviewed and merged independently.

## Why This Phase Exists

Every other phase needs to read DIRECTUS_URL, DIRECTUS_TOKEN, etc. from the environment. Without typed env declarations, TypeScript will flag every import.meta.env access. Without .env.example, developers cloning the template won't know what variables to set. Without remotePatterns in astro.config.mjs, Astro will refuse to optimize Directus remote images.

The diagnostic logger is here (not in Phase 2) because the client, cache, and provider modules all need to log through it from day one. Building it last would mean retrofitting redaction into every console.log call.

## Deliverables

1. .env.example — committed, empty placeholders only (no URLs, tokens, or infrastructure hints)
2. src/env.d.ts — TypeScript declarations for all Directus env vars including DIRECTUS_REQUIRED
3. .gitignore updates — .cache/ entry (prd/ already added)
4. astro.config.mjs — image.remotePatterns with protocol-only pattern (generic, works with any instance)
5. Diagnostic logger utility — redact() function, structured [directus] prefix logging

## Security Note

The .env.example file is the single most dangerous file in this phase. It will be committed to a public repo. It MUST contain only empty placeholders. No sample URLs like 'https://example-cms.com', no hint tokens like 'your-token-here'. Empty strings only. The PR reviewer should verify this character by character.

## PRD Reference: Sections 1.1–1.6, 2.2

## Acceptance Criteria

- The requirements in this bead are implemented without expanding scope beyond the named behavior, files, or phase.
- Local template behavior still works when Directus environment variables are unset; strict failures only occur when DIRECTUS_REQUIRED=true or when this bead explicitly scopes strict-mode validation.

- Relevant tests, docs, and build/check commands are added or updated; any command that cannot pass has a follow-up blocker bead with exact failure context.

title: Add remote image patterns to astro.config.mjs
description:
## Overview

Configure Astro's image optimization to accept remote images from any HTTPS source. This enables Astro's <Image /> component to download, optimize (WebP/AVIF), and include Directus asset images in the static build.

## Requirements

Add to astro.config.mjs:
```javascript
image: {
  remotePatterns: [
    { protocol: 'https' }
  ],
},
```

## Why protocol-only (not domain-specific)

Using just { protocol: 'https' } instead of a hardcoded domain keeps the config generic — it works with ANY Directus instance URL. Hardcoding 'cms.choostring.ventures' would:
1. Leak infrastructure info in the public repo
2. Break for anyone using a different Directus instance
3. Require a code change when migrating CMS hosts

## Prerequisite

Directus file permissions must allow public read access to assets used in published content. If assets require auth, Astro's image optimization will fail to download them — this is intentional (fail-safe over fail-open). Documented in PRD Section 9 migration guide.

## Performance Note

First build with remote images will be slower than subsequent builds — Astro caches optimized images in node_modules/.astro/. This is normal and expected.

title: Create diagnostic logger with redact() for all Directus output
description:
## Overview

Build the diagnostic logging utility that ALL Directus module console output passes through. The core function is redact() — it replaces any occurrence of DIRECTUS_URL, DIRECTUS_TOKEN, and DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG values in any string before it reaches the console.

## Requirements

Create a logging utility (likely src/lib/directus/logger.ts or similar) with:

1. redact(message: string): string — Replaces env var values with masked versions:
   - DIRECTUS_URL value → 'https://cms.***'
   - DIRECTUS_TOKEN value → '***'
   - DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG value → '****-slug' (partial mask preserving length hint)

2. logDirectusDiagnostic(stats): void — Structured build output:
   - Source status (live/cache/local/not configured)
   - Content counts per collection
   - Cache operations (written/read/rejected)
   - Fetch timing

3. All log functions (info, warn, error) pass through redact() before console output

## Why This Is Security-Critical

This is a PUBLIC repo. Build logs from GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Pages, and Vercel are often visible in PR checks or deployment logs. Error messages from failed API calls can contain the Directus URL (e.g., 'Fetch failed: 401 Unauthorized from https://cms.choostring.ventures/items/blog_articles'). Without redaction, any build failure exposes infrastructure.

The redact() function is also used by the audit script (Phase 6) and the verify script (Phase 2). Building it early means every module gets redaction from day one.

## Considerations

- redact() should handle the case where env vars are empty/undefined (no-op)
- redact() should not crash if the value appears in a URL-encoded form
- The function should be importable from a standalone module with no heavy dependencies
- Console output format: [directus] prefix for all messages

## Example Output

On success:
  [directus] Source: live (connected)
  [directus] Site slug: ****-choo (redacted)
  [directus] Blog: 3 articles, 2 categories
  [directus] Cache: written to .cache/directus-blog.json

On failure:
  [directus] Fetch failed: 401 Unauthorized (https://cms.***)
  [directus] Blog: using cache (2h stale)

Not configured:
  [directus] Not configured — using local content

## Overview

description:
## Overview

Define the shared view model interfaces that are the contract of the content provider pattern. Local adapters and Directus normalization modules must produce these types, and pages should only consume these types instead of raw Directus records or Astro `CollectionEntry` objects.

## Requirements

Create `src/lib/content/types.ts` with:

1. `ImageMeta`
   - `{ url: string, alt?: string, width?: number, height?: number }`
   - Carries dimensions and alt text from Directus file relations for Astro image rendering.

2. `BlogPost`
   - `content: string` is raw markdown/text and must not be pre-rendered HTML because reading-time and excerpts depend on raw content.
   - `rendered?: { html: string, headings: { depth: number; slug: string; text: string }[] }` is present only for CMS content rendered by the markdown pipeline.
   - `tags: string[]` from local frontmatter or an empty array for CMS until CMS tags are explicitly added.
   - `categories: string[]` from local frontmatter or the CMS category relation name.
   - `category?: { name: string; slug: string }` for structured CMS category routing.
   - `seo?: { titleTag?: string; metaDescription?: string; canonicalUrl?: string; robots?: string }`.
   - `sitemapEligible: boolean`, false for noindex or external canonical URLs.
   - `isDraft: boolean`.

3. `BlogCategory`
   - `{ name: string; slug: string; description?: string; postCount: number }`.

4. `Location`
   - Supports both existing local `locations.json` entries and richer Directus `cities` records.
   - Include: `slug`, `city`, `state?`, `heading?`, `description`, `longDescription?`, `longDescriptionHtml?`, `address?`, `phone?`, `seo?`, `stats?`, `faqs?`, `coordinates?`, `operatingHours?`, `serviceAreaKeywords?`.
   - `longDescription` stays raw/plain text or markdown-compatible source text.
   - `longDescriptionHtml` is sanitized rendered HTML from CMS markdown only.
   - `faqs` entries should support `{ question: string; answer: string; answerHtml?: string }` so pages do not confuse raw answers with sanitized HTML.

## Critical Constraints

- Raw content fields must never contain unsanitized HTML from Directus.
- Rendered HTML fields must only be produced by the CMS markdown pipeline with the custom sanitization schema.
- Pages should branch on the presence of rendered fields, not on a source-name enum.
- Local fallback data must be representable without fake CMS-only fields.

## Source Mapping Documentation

Document these mappings in code comments or a companion markdown note:

- Local blog: tags/categories from frontmatter; author from the team reference slug; rendered content remains undefined.
- CMS blog: category from relation; tags empty until explicitly modeled; rendered content comes from the sanitized markdown pipeline.
- Local locations: map existing `src/content/locations/locations.json` and `locations.schema.ts` output into `Location`; address/phone/coordinates/operating-hours fields stay available.
- CMS cities: map Directus city fields into `Location`; missing address/phone/coordinates/operating-hours remain optional and pages render graceful fallbacks.

- Type definitions compile under the repo's strict TypeScript settings without forcing pages to use raw Directus or Astro collection types.

- Raw markdown/text fields and sanitized HTML fields are separate for CMS-rendered location content.
- Local no-Directus builds keep current blog and location routes functional.

## Requirements

Create src/lib/directus/client.ts with:

1. isDirectusConfigured(): boolean — checks Boolean(import.meta.env.DIRECTUS_URL)

2. createClient(url, token?) — SDK setup with bearer auth via REST interceptor. Adapted from arp-astro (src/lib/directus.ts lines 67-81).

3. fetchWithTimeout<T>(fn, timeoutMs=15000) — Race-based timeout using AbortController. Adapted from arp-astro lines 83-102.

4. fetchPublishedArticles(timeoutMs?) → DirectusFetchOutcome<DirectusBlogArticle>
   - Filters: status=published, site.slug=DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG
   - Fields: explicit ARTICLE_FIELDS list (pinned, not *)

- ARTICLE_FIELDS is an explicit const array listing every field to fetch. This prevents: (a) accidentally fetching sensitive fields, (b) schema changes silently adding unexpected data, (c) over-fetching fields we don't use.
- Bearer auth uses REST interceptor pattern (onRequest callback) rather than the SDK's built-in auth, matching the arp-astro approach.
- Error handling wraps all SDK calls in try/catch and returns DirectusFetchOutcome — never throws. The provider decides what to do with errors.
- Draft mode is client-level, not provider-level, because the filter change happens in the SDK query, not in post-processing.

- The SDK's TypeScript generics are complex. You'll likely need 'as never' casts on readItems calls. This is a known SDK workaround, not a code smell.
- All error messages from this module must pass through redact() (from the diagnostic logger) before reaching the console.

## Overview

Build the asset URL resolution and token safety module. This is a security-critical module — it's the primary defense against Directus tokens appearing in the built HTML output.

## Requirements

Create src/lib/directus/assets.ts with:

1. resolveAssetUrl(file, externalUrl, alt?, options?) → ResolvedAsset | null
   - Dual-source resolution: prefer Directus file relation, fall back to legacy string URL
   - If file (DirectusFile object): resolve to ${DIRECTUS_ASSET_BASE_URL}/assets/${file.id}
   - If externalUrl (string): validate via isSafePublicUrl(), return as-is
   - Extract alt text: explicit alt param > file.description > file.title
   - Extract dimensions: file.width, file.height (from DirectusFile)

2. isSafePublicUrl(url: string): boolean
   - Reject dangerous protocols: javascript:, data:, vbscript: (case-insensitive)
   - Also check for token leakage (calls isTokenSafe internally)
   - Use regex /^(javascript|data|vbscript):/i for protocol check
   - Handle URL parse failures gracefully (return false)

3. isTokenSafe(url: string): boolean
   - Reject URLs containing access_token or token query parameters
   - Check both parsed URL searchParams and regex fallback for malformed URLs
   - Pattern: /[?&](?:access_token|token)=/i

4. assertNoTokenLeakage(urls: string[]): void
   - Throws if ANY URL in the array fails isTokenSafe()
   - Called during normalization on all resolved asset URLs
   - Error message includes the field name (e.g., 'Token leak detected in og_image URL') but NOT the actual URL value

## Security Design

- assertNoTokenLeakage() is a HARD FAIL — if a token leaks into an asset URL, the build must stop. This is not a warning.
- The error message MUST NOT include the leaked URL (that would log the token). Include only the field name and article slug.
- isSafePublicUrl() is defense-in-depth against CMS content containing dangerous protocol links. The markdown sanitizer (rehype-sanitize) also strips these, but the asset resolver catches them at the data layer.

title: Create markdown renderer with custom sanitization schema
description:
## Overview

Build the unified/remark/rehype markdown rendering pipeline for Directus CMS content. This module is used ONLY for CMS-sourced markdown — local content uses Astro's built-in renderer. The sanitization schema is a security boundary for CMS-authored content.

## Requirements

Create src/lib/directus/markdown.ts with:

1. renderMarkdown(content: string, options?): { html: string, headings: Heading[] }
   - Pipeline: remarkParse → remarkGfm → remarkRehype (allowDangerousHtml: false) → rehypeSanitize (CUSTOM schema) → rehypeSlug → rehypeStringify
   - Heading extraction: collect h2-h4 during processing, return as array for TOC
   - Processor cached at module level (created once per build, reused for all articles)

2. Custom sanitization schema (CRITICAL — do NOT use default):
   The default rehype-sanitize schema strips class attributes, id attributes, and target on links. This breaks syntax highlighting, heading anchors, and external links. Use a custom schema:

   Allowed tags: p, h1-h6, ul, ol, li, strong, em, blockquote, pre, code, hr, br, table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td, img, a, figure, figcaption + GFM: del, ins, details, summary, input

   Allowed attributes:
   - a: href (protocols: http, https, mailto, tel), target, rel
   - img: src (protocols: http, https ONLY — no data: URIs), alt, width, height
   - code: className matching /^language-/ (syntax highlighting)
   - span: className matching /^hljs-/ (Shiki token classes)
   - * (global): id (heading anchors from rehype-slug)

   Stripped: script, style, all on* event handlers, javascript:/data:/vbscript: protocols

## Why allowDangerousHtml: false

The remarkRehype plugin has an allowDangerousHtml option. Setting it to false means raw HTML in markdown source is dropped, not passed through. Since CMS content might contain author-injected HTML, we NEVER pass it through — the sanitizer handles what tags/attributes are allowed. This is defense in depth.

## Why Custom Schema (Not Default)

The default schema from hast-util-sanitize is designed for untrusted user-generated content (like blog comments). It's too restrictive for editorial CMS content:
- Strips className → breaks syntax highlighting classes (language-typescript, hljs-keyword)
- Strips id → breaks rehype-slug heading anchors
- Strips target → breaks external links opening in new tabs
- Strips data: on img src → already handled (good), but also strips some valid patterns

Our custom schema allows these specific patterns while still stripping scripts, styles, and event handlers.

## Considerations

- The processor MUST be cached at module level (not created per article). unified().use().use()... is expensive to set up. Create once, process() many times.
- Called during normalization (normalize.ts), not at page level. The result is stored in BlogPost.rendered.
- Heading extraction should capture depth (2-4), slug (from rehype-slug), and text content.

title: Create disk cache module with slug validation
description:
## Overview

Build the disk cache layer that sits between the Directus client and the content provider. The cache enables offline development, speeds up repeated builds, and serves as the second tier in the CMS-Preferred Fallback Chain (Live → Cache → Local).

## Requirements

Create src/lib/directus/cache.ts with:

1. readCache<T>(collection: string): CachedData<T> | null
   - Reads from CACHE_DIR/directus-{collection}.json
   - Validates the cached site slug matches the current DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG
   - If slugs don't match: log warning, return null (treat as cache miss)
   - If file doesn't exist or is corrupt JSON: return null
   - Returns: { data: T[], cachedAt: string, siteSlug: string }

2. writeCache<T>(collection: string, data: T[], siteSlug: string): void
   - Writes to CACHE_DIR/directus-{collection}.json
   - Creates CACHE_DIR if it doesn't exist (mkdir -p equivalent)
   - Includes siteSlug and cachedAt timestamp in the JSON

3. CachedData<T> interface: { data: T[], cachedAt: string, siteSlug: string }

## Why Slug Validation Is Critical

Without slug validation, this scenario is possible:
1. Developer works on site-A (DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG=site-a), cache populates
2. Developer switches to site-B (DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG=site-b), CMS is down
3. Cache returns site-A content for site-B → content contamination

The slug validation ensures cached data is ONLY used when it matches the current site context. A mismatch is treated as a cache miss and logged.

## Considerations

- CACHE_DIR defaults to .cache if env var not set
- Cache files are JSON — include a _meta field with { version: 1, siteSlug, cachedAt } for future schema evolution
- Cache is ALWAYS cold in Cloudflare Pages production (ephemeral build containers) — this is expected and documented in PRD
- Reading/writing should use fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync (build-time only, sync is fine)
- All log output passes through the diagnostic logger (redact() applied)

## Overview

This is the most complex single task in the entire integration. The blog detail page must be substantially rewritten to:
1. Get content from the provider (source-agnostic)
2. Handle dual rendering paths (CMS pre-rendered HTML vs Astro native render)
3. Resolve author references to full team data
4. Generate static paths for both local and CMS posts

## Requirements

Rewrite src/pages/blog/[slug].astro:

### getStaticPaths()
- Replace getCollection('blog') with getBlogPosts()
- Map posts to { params: { slug }, props: { post } }
- Each post is a BlogPost object, not CollectionEntry

### Content Rendering (the critical dual path)
```astro
---
// If post has pre-rendered CMS content
if (post.rendered) {
  // Use rendered.html directly — already sanitized by the markdown pipeline
  // Use rendered.headings for TOC
} else {
  // Local content — use Astro's native render()
  // Need to get the entry from the content collection by slug
  const entry = await getEntry('blog', post.slug)
  const { Content, headings } = await entry.render()
}
---
```

### Author Resolution
- post.author is { slug: string } — resolve to full team member data
- Use getEntry('team', post.author.slug) or equivalent

### Field Migration Table (from PRD)
- post.data.title → post.title
- post.data.description → post.description
- post.data.pubDate → post.pubDate
- post.data.image → post.image (ImageMeta | string | undefined)
- post.body → post.content (raw markdown, for reading time only)

- BlogPostingLD: title, description, pubDate, image (ImageMeta), author

1. The current page uses CollectionEntry<'blog'> which has a .render() method — BlogPost doesn't

description:
## Overview

Build the normalization module that transforms raw DirectusBlogArticle objects into the shared BlogPost view model. This is the critical bridge between CMS data and page components — it handles date parsing, asset resolution, markdown rendering, SEO computation, and draft detection.

## Requirements

Create src/lib/directus/normalize.ts with:

1. normalizeArticle(raw: DirectusBlogArticle): BlogPost
   Transform each field:
   - slug: raw.slug (passthrough)
   - title: raw.title (passthrough)
   - description: raw.short_description ?? ''
   - pubDate: new Date(raw.date_published ?? raw.date_created)
   - updatedDate: raw.date_updated ? new Date(raw.date_updated) : undefined
   - content: raw.content ?? '' (raw markdown — NOT rendered)
   - rendered: renderMarkdown(raw.content ?? '') → { html, headings }
   - image: resolveAssetUrl(raw.featured_image_file, raw.featured_image, 'Featured image')
   - ogImage: resolveAssetUrl(raw.og_image_file, raw.og_image, 'OG image')
   - twitterImage: resolveAssetUrl(raw.twitter_image_file, raw.twitter_image)
   - author: { slug: raw.author_slug } (deferred resolution — page resolves to full author)
   - tags: [] (deferred — CMS articles don't have tags yet)
   - categories: raw.category ? [raw.category.name] : []
   - category: raw.category ? { name: raw.category.name, slug: raw.category.slug } : undefined
   - isDraft: raw.status === 'draft'
   - seo: { titleTag, metaDescription, canonicalUrl, robots } from raw
   - sitemapEligible: computed from robots + canonicalUrl
   - showToc: true (default for CMS articles)

2. normalizeArticles(raws: DirectusBlogArticle[]): BlogPost[]
   - Maps normalizeArticle over array
   - Calls assertNoTokenLeakage on all resolved asset URLs (batch check)
   - Logs count and any skipped articles (e.g., missing slug)

3. normalizeCategories(raws: DirectusBlogCategory[]): BlogCategory[]

- content: ALWAYS raw markdown. calculateReadingTime() depends on word-counting raw text.
- rendered: { html, headings } — produced by calling renderMarkdown() from the markdown module.

## Overview

Build the local content adapter that converts Astro CollectionEntry<'blog'> objects into the shared BlogPost type. This ensures the template works IDENTICALLY without Directus — local markdown files produce the same view model as CMS content.

## Requirements

Create src/lib/content/local.ts with:

1. getLocalBlogPosts(): Promise<BlogPost[]>
   - Calls getCollection('blog') from astro:content
   - Filters out drafts (post.data.draft === true) in production
   - Maps each CollectionEntry<'blog'> to BlogPost:
     - slug: entry.id (or entry.slug depending on Astro 5.x content layer)
     - title, description, pubDate, updatedDate: from entry.data
     - content: entry.body (raw markdown)
     - rendered: undefined (local posts use Astro's native render() in pages)
     - image: entry.data.image ? { url: entry.data.image } as ImageMeta : undefined
     - author: { slug: entry.data.author } (reference ID from frontmatter)
     - tags: entry.data.tags ?? []
     - categories: entry.data.categories ?? []
     - isDraft: entry.data.draft ?? false
     - showToc: entry.data.showToc ?? false
     - seo: undefined (local posts don't have SEO overrides)

title: Create content provider with CMS-preferred fallback chain
description:
## Overview

Build the content provider: the single entry point that pages use for blog content. The provider implements the CMS-preferred fallback chain and module-level memoization. Pages import `getBlogPosts()`, `getBlogCategories()`, and related helpers without knowing whether data came from Directus, cache, or local content.

## Requirements

Create `src/lib/content/provider.ts` with:

1. `getBlogPosts(): Promise<BlogPost[]>`
   - If Directus is not configured, return `getLocalBlogPosts()` and skip CMS entirely.
   - If live `fetchPublishedArticles()` succeeds, normalize articles, write cache, and return CMS posts.
   - If live fetch fails, try a site-slug-validated blog cache.
   - If `DIRECTUS_REQUIRED=true`, throw instead of using cache/local fallback unless the strict-mode design in the reconciled PRD says otherwise.
   - Otherwise fall back to `getLocalBlogPosts()`.
   - Log the selected tier through the redacted diagnostic logger.

2. `getBlogCategories(): Promise<BlogCategory[]>`
   - Use the same active source-tier principle as posts.
   - If Directus is not configured, derive categories from local posts/frontmatter.
   - If live/cache CMS categories are available, normalize those categories and compute `postCount` from the active CMS post set.
   - If CMS categories are unavailable but the active post set has category names, derive categories from that active post set.
   - Do not merge local fallback categories with live CMS categories during normal operation; mixed-source category pages are surprising and make counts hard to explain.

3. `getBlogPostBySlug(slug: string): Promise<BlogPost | undefined>`
   - Uses memoized `getBlogPosts()` and finds by slug.

4. `getRelatedPosts(post: BlogPost, limit?: number): Promise<BlogPost[]>`
   - Calls the refactored related-posts utility with shared `BlogPost` types.

## Memoization

Each getter stores its promise at module level so one build performs at most one API request per collection/source path regardless of how many pages import the provider.

## Strict Mode

When `DIRECTUS_REQUIRED=true`, failures should be explicit, redacted, and actionable. The reconciled PRD must decide whether strict mode can use a validated cache; if not, strict mode should fail on unreachable live CMS instead of serving stale content.

## Per-Content-Area Independence

Blog and locations have independent fallback chains. Blog can use live CMS while locations use local fallback, and vice versa, without failing unrelated pages.

## PRD Reference

Must be reconciled by `astro-template-directus-integration-rb2.7.1` before implementation.

- `getBlogPosts()` and `getBlogCategories()` return local content when Directus is not configured.
- Live CMS blog content does not silently merge with local fallback blog content.
- Category counts are computed from the same active post source tier used to render posts.
- Provider diagnostics identify the selected tier without leaking secrets or concrete Directus instance URLs.

Update `Header.astro` so the Locations nav link reflects provider data availability after the full fallback chain, not just live CMS availability. If local fallback locations exist, the link should remain visible when Directus is unset.

## Requirements

Modify `src/components/Header.astro`:

1. Import `getLocations()` from the content provider.
2. Resolve locations in frontmatter and conditionally include `{ text: 'Locations', href: '/locations', exact: false }` when `locations.length > 0`.
3. Apply the same condition to desktop and mobile nav rendering.
4. Rely on provider memoization so the Header does not trigger repeated Directus requests across pages.
5. Preserve the current nav item when local fallback data has locations.

This adds a provider call to Header frontmatter during build. The provider must memoize per content area so the build performs at most one locations fetch/fallback resolution.

## Considerations

- The listing page remains safe and shows an empty state even if the nav link is hidden.
- This is a template UX improvement: users should not see a Locations nav item only when there is no location data, and they should not lose it just because they are using the local fallback.

## File

Modify: `src/components/Header.astro`

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Locations nav link is visible with existing local `locations.json` data when Directus is unset.
- The link is visible with CMS/cache locations and hidden only when the provider returns an empty array.
- Desktop and mobile navs use the same condition.

title: Create build output audit script for token leakage
description:
## Overview

Create a post-build audit script that scans the entire dist/ output for leaked Directus tokens, URLs, and other sensitive patterns. This is the last line of defense — if token redaction or sanitization failed anywhere, this script catches it.

## Requirements

Create scripts/audit-build.mjs:

1. Scan all files in dist/ recursively (.html, .xml, .json, .js)
2. Search for patterns:
   - DIRECTUS_TOKEN value (from env)
   - DIRECTUS_URL value (from env)
   - DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG value (from env)
   - Generic patterns: access_token=, Bearer , authorization: (case-insensitive)
   - Known Directus URL patterns: /items/, /assets/ with token params

3. Output:
   - If clean: 'Build audit PASSED: no sensitive patterns found in dist/'
   - If found: list each file + line number + pattern type (NOT the actual value)
   - Exit code: 0 if clean, 1 if any findings

4. Integration:
   - Add as postbuild script in package.json: 'postbuild': 'node scripts/audit-build.mjs'
   - Runs automatically after every 'pnpm build'

## Why Post-Build (Not Just Runtime)

Runtime redaction (redact() in logger) protects console output. The build audit protects the DEPLOYED output. Even if redaction works perfectly, a bug in asset resolution or markdown rendering could embed a token in an HTML attribute or JSON-LD block. The audit catches what runtime missed.

## Considerations

- Must handle binary files gracefully (skip images, fonts)
- Scan only text-based files: .html, .xml, .json, .js, .css, .txt
- Performance: dist/ is typically small (<100 files for a static site) — brute force scan is fine
- The script reads env vars to know what patterns to search for — if env vars aren't set, it still searches for generic patterns (access_token=, etc.)
- Exit code 1 blocks deployment in CI pipelines

## File

Modify: package.json (add postbuild script)

title: Create E2E build integration test suite (multi-config matrix)
description:
## Overview

Create a comprehensive E2E test suite that builds the site under multiple environment configurations and validates the output. This is the ultimate integration test — it proves the entire system works end-to-end, from env vars through the provider to the generated HTML.

The existing tests/build.test.ts verifies a single build succeeds. This suite tests MULTIPLE configurations: local-only, CMS-live, CMS-unreachable, and strict-mode. It also validates output content (not just exit codes).

## Requirements

Create tests/e2e/build-integration.test.ts:

### Test Suite Structure:

#### Scenario 1: Local-Only Mode (PRIMARY — most users' first experience)
```
Config: DIRECTUS_URL='' (empty), all other DIRECTUS_* vars empty
Expected:
- Build succeeds (exit 0)
- dist/blog/index.html exists and contains local post titles
- dist/rss.xml is valid XML with <item> entries
- dist/ contains NO Directus URLs or tokens (audit check)
- [directus] logs show 'Not configured — using local content'
```

#### Scenario 2: CMS-Live Mode (requires DIRECTUS_* vars set in CI secrets or .env)
```
Config: DIRECTUS_URL set, DIRECTUS_TOKEN set, DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG set
Expected (if CMS reachable):
- Build succeeds
- dist/blog/ contains CMS article pages (slugs from Directus)
- CMS post pages contain rendered HTML (not raw markdown)
- dist/ contains NO tokens (audit check — this is the critical case)
- .cache/ directory created with directus-blog.json
- [directus] logs show 'Source: live (connected)'
Skip if: DIRECTUS_URL not set in CI environment (graceful skip, not failure)
```

#### Scenario 3: CMS-Unreachable Fallback
```
Config: DIRECTUS_URL='https://invalid.example.com:9999', DIRECTUS_TOKEN='fake'
Expected:
- Build succeeds (fallback to local content)
- dist/blog/ contains local post pages (not CMS)
- [directus] logs show fetch error + fallback message
- Build does NOT hang (timeout enforced)
```

#### Scenario 4: Strict Mode Failure
```
Config: DIRECTUS_URL='https://invalid.example.com:9999', DIRECTUS_REQUIRED='true'
Expected:
- Build FAILS (non-zero exit)
- Error message mentions 'Directus CMS required but unreachable'
- Error message does NOT contain the invalid URL (redacted)
```

#### Scenario 5: Token Leakage Audit (post-build)
```
Config: Same as Scenario 2 (if CMS available)
Expected:
- Run scripts/audit-build.mjs against dist/
- Exit 0 (no findings)
- Scan all .html, .xml, .json files for DIRECTUS_TOKEN value → none found
- Scan for generic patterns (access_token=, Bearer) → none found
```

### Implementation Notes:

1. Each scenario runs in a subprocess with modified env vars (child_process.execSync with custom env)
2. Use separate temp dirs for dist/ output between scenarios (prevent cross-contamination)
3. Set generous timeouts: 120s per build (Astro builds can be slow with remote images)
4. The existing tests/build.test.ts can remain as-is (quick smoke test)

### Logging Requirements (CRITICAL — user specifically requested detailed logging):

- Log each scenario start: '[E2E] === Scenario 1: Local-Only Mode ==='
- Log env vars being used (REDACTED): '[E2E] DIRECTUS_URL=(empty) DIRECTUS_TOKEN=(empty)'
- Log build command: '[E2E] Running: pnpm build'
- Log build duration: '[E2E] Build completed in 12.3s'
- Log each assertion: '[E2E] PASS: dist/blog/index.html exists'
- Log assertion failures with full context: '[E2E] FAIL: Expected dist/blog/index.html to contain "My First Post" but got: <actual content snippet>'
- Log scenario summary: '[E2E] Scenario 1: 5/5 assertions passed'
- Log final summary: '[E2E] === RESULTS: 4/5 scenarios passed, 1 skipped (CMS not configured) ==='

### Vitest Configuration:

Add to vitest.config.ts or create separate config:
- Exclude tests/e2e/** from default 'pnpm test' run
- Add script: 'test:e2e': 'vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.ts'
- E2E tests should NOT run on every commit — only on PR or manual trigger

## File

Create: vitest.e2e.config.ts (extends base config, includes e2e tests)
